land.text: the Pandya country around Madurai; 'Pandya records describe the Kalabhras defeating the Cholas, Pandyas, and Cheras'

successors.note: The Pandya dynasty (Cliopatria 'Pandya Dynasty', 592-921) is the later revival that, on the Kalabhra page, 'defeated and ended' the Kalabhra rule with the Pallavas and Chalukyas; no state holds this land in Cliopatria between 306 and 591.

capitals.name: Madurai
capitals.note: The page says the capital was Korkai 'initially' and 'later moved to Koodal (now Madurai) during the reign of Nedunjeliyan I', with no date; Madurai stands for the whole life. Coordinates are the gazetteer's Madurai.

keyframe_review.note: 32,600 km2 for -291..298 (Madurai, Tirunelveli and Ramanathapuram, 77.2-79.3 E, 8.1-10.3 N). The infobox gives no area; it says the kingdom 'extended between Travancore in the west, Vellaru river in the north and all the way to the ocean in the east and the south'. The shape fits the north (10.3 N) and the sea; its west edge is the Ghats, with Travancore itself outside. Ashoka's 2nd and 13th rock edicts 'place' the Pandyas 'outside the southern boundary of the Mauryan Empire'. No dated change on the page.
Same outline as -291 (32,600 km2) for 299..305; the page gives no reason for the split at 299 and no end date for the dynasty. Unverified beyond the first keyframe.

region.text: the Pandya country: between Travancore in the west, the Vellaru river in the north and the ocean in the east and south, with Madurai

ledger.note: The Pandyas exist by 291 BCE. The page gives no founding date: it says kings are 'frequently mentioned in Sangam literature of the third century BCE and onwards', that the 2nd and 13th rock edicts of Ashoka (273-232 BCE) mention the Pandyas, and that Mudukudumi Peruvaludhi's coins 'have been dated to around 200 BCE'. The year is Cliopatria's first shape.

region.text: the Pandya country at the end of the Sangam age

ledger.note: c. 305: the Early Pandyas end in Cliopatria. The Early Pandyas page does not say when or how they ended. The Kalabhra page: 'Pandya records describe the Kalabhras defeating the Cholas, Pandyas, and Cheras', undated; the Kalabhras ruled 'sometime between the 3rd century and 6th century CE'.

certainty.note: The page gives the kingdom's limits as a river and the sea and a region (Travancore), not as a line; the Mauryan boundary in the edicts is a statement of 'beyond the borders', not a frontier.

sources.title: Early Pandyas
sources.note: Infobox extent (Travancore to Vellaru river), capitals Korkai and Madurai, kings, coins c. 200 BCE, Hathigumpha c. 150 BCE, Roman embassy c. 13 CE; no area, no end date.

sources.title: Kalabhra dynasty
sources.note: Kalabhras between the 3rd and 6th century CE; Pandya records of the Kalabhras defeating the three kings; no date.

notes:
Group sa-02-a. Pages: Early Pandyas and Kalabhra dynasty (two; the budget is 1-2).

THIN. The Early Pandyas page dates no territory, no frontier and no end: its dated items are Ashoka's edicts (273-232 BCE), the Hathigumpha inscription (c. 150 BCE, tribute from the Pandya king), Mudukudumi Peruvaludhi's coins (c. 200 BCE), the Roman embassy (c. 13 CE) and Julian's embassy (c. 361 CE). The founding and the end are confidence 1 (Cliopatria's -291 and 305). The Early Pandyas are separate from the later Pandya Dynasty (592-921) and Pandya Empire (1216-1325) in Cliopatria; the Kalabhra interregnum lies between.

UNDATED, NOT ENTERED. Nedunjeliyan II's victory at Talaialanganam over a coalition of Cheras, Cholas and five other kings (Tanjore district); Nedunjeliyan III's advance into the Chola southern province and the Chera eastern province; Pudappandiyan's conquest of Ollaiyur (near Pudukkottai); Musiri Mutriya Cheliyan's conquest of Musiri; the move of the capital from Korkai to Madurai. The Chera page adds that Nedunjeliyan II captured the Chera king Mantharam Cheral Irumporai 'in the early 3rd century CE'. None of these gives a year or a border, so no ledger event or war entry was made.

GAZETTEER. All names exist (Madurai is a place; the others are Cliopatria shapes). Korkai is not a gazetteer place.
